facts.raw_span: A 5‐year‐9‐month‐old, 170‐kg domestic llama mare was referred for a 1‐week history of dyspnea and inspiratory noise
dyspnea and inspiratory noise
a 10 × 8 × 3‐cm subcutaneous mass that was partially firm and fluctuant, slightly painful, and mildly warm
the overlying skin appeared normal
No dysphagia, other masses, or lymphadenopathy were detected
mild leukocytosis (23,690/µL; reference 8,700–17,500/µL)
neutrophilia (92.4%; reference 42.4–76.4%)
lymphopenia (3.0%; reference 7.0–32.5%)
eosinophils were decreased
Flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea under sedation revealed no abnormalities
Cervical ultrasonography showed a well‐demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass
Thoracic and cervical radiographs demonstrated a ventral soft‐tissue‐density mass in the mid‐to‐caudal cervical region causing a mild mass effect on the trachea
